commit_scope: Root cause and heal of the API's ten-minute CPU window after every start: /api/inventory/flow looked up the active task for every blocked idea with a full scan of the in-memory task store (4,600 ideas × thousands of tasks, 91 s of CPU per build, rebuilt every 30 s under page loads); the flow now builds one fingerprint index per build and the three smaller candidate loops use the same.
evidence_refs: Observed in production's log of its last start (2026-10-20 09:53 UTC): in the first twelve minutes /api/inventory/flow was requested 8 times with durations up to 292 s while every other route read 3–14 s; the API container sat at ~100 % CPU on two threads; the web's specs, contributors and demo pages request that route on load.

Read in api/app/routers/inventory.py: the flow is memoized 30 s per argument tuple (ttl_cached); api/app/services/inventory_service.py builds it per request. The body's own timing instrument (inventory.timing_enabled) run once inside the production container (docker exec, PYTHONPATH=/app, a separate process): elapsed 92,966 ms, of which unblock_sort=91,381 ms — a timer that spans the per-idea loop above the sort. compat rows 0.6 s; every other stage under 1.3 s.

In that loop, for every blocked idea: agent_service.find_active_task_by_fingerprint(fingerprint) — which calls _ensure_store_loaded and then scans every task in the in-memory store (api/app/services/agent_service_active_task.py) comparing context.task_fingerprint. Ideas × tasks, pure CPU: the window. The per-call cache in the loop keyed by fingerprint never hit, since fingerprints are unique per idea.

Heal: active_tasks_by_fingerprint() — one pass over the store, active tasks indexed by fingerprint — exported through agent_service; the flow loop and the three candidate loops (inventory_service 913 and 1738, inventory/spec_discovery 349) read the index. find_active_task_by_fingerprint stays for single lookups.

Proof: test_service_claim_and_fingerprint_dedup asserts the index holds the active fingerprint and not the completed one; the flow built through the route with find_active_task_by_fingerprint replaced by a function that raises — 200, 0 per-idea lookups, 33 queue rows (local data). Locally the flow takes 0.2 s against sqlite; the production number after rollout is the live check: api container CPU in the first ten minutes after start, and /api/inventory/flow under a few seconds.
The 30 s memo and the request stampede stay as they are: with a build of a second or two they are harmless; a longer memo would hide live changes to the queue.
